title: 8 Best Financial Reporting Software Tools in 2026
summary: Compare the 8 best financial reporting software tools in 2026, from Workiva and OneStream to AI agents like Concourse, by reporting strength, fit, and cost.
body_markdown:
"Financial reporting software" is a deceptively broad category. It covers tools that file your 10-K with the SEC, tools that assemble the monthly board deck, tools that consolidate dozens of entities at close, and tools that pull live numbers out of your ERP into Excel. They are all called financial reporting software, and they are not interchangeable, which is exactly why choosing one is confusing.


This guide compares the eight best financial reporting software tools in 2026, from enterprise disclosure and consolidation platforms like Workiva and OneStream to Excel-native FP&A tools like Vena and Datarails, plus the newer wave of AI agents that *produce* the reporting rather than give you another place to build it. We break down what each is genuinely best at, so you can match the tool to the report you actually need to produce.


## **What is the best financial reporting software?**


> The best financial reporting software in 2026 depends on the report: Concourse for teams that want AI agents to produce management and board reporting end to end, Workiva for SEC and statutory disclosure, OneStream for enterprise close and consolidation, Planful and Vena for FP&A and management reporting, Cube and Datarails for spreadsheet-native teams, and insightsoftware for operational ERP reporting.


> **Concourse is the AI-agent option on this list.** Instead of another surface you build reports in, Concourse deploys autonomous finance agents that connect to your ERP, data warehouse, and billing systems and produce management, board, and variance reporting on a schedule or on request, with every number traceable back to source. It is built for finance teams that want AI to do the reporting work, not just visualize it.


## **How we evaluated financial reporting software**


Because "financial reporting" means different things to different teams, we compared these tools across the criteria that actually change the decision:


- **Reporting type.** External/statutory disclosure (SEC, XBRL), management and board reporting, consolidation, or operational ERP reporting, tools specialize in different ones.
- **Data connectivity.** How well it pulls from your ERP, data warehouse, and source systems into a trusted, single version of the numbers.
- **Automation vs. manual assembly.** Whether the tool helps a person build the report, or produces it for them.
- **Traceability.** Whether every figure ties back to source, the thing that makes reporting defensible to a board or auditor.
- **AI capability.** From a copilot over your data to autonomous agents that generate the reporting.
- **Fit and ideal size.** From SMB and advisory to global enterprise and public companies.

## **The 8 best financial reporting software tools in 2026**


### **1. Concourse, Best for AI Agents That Produce Reporting**


Concourse is an AI agent platform for corporate finance. Rather than another surface to build reports in, it connects directly to your ERP, data warehouse, and billing systems and produces the reporting itself: management and board packages, variance and flux commentary, and ad hoc analysis, on a schedule or on request.


What sets it apart from a build-it-yourself reporting tool is the execution model. Concourse does not just centralize your data for an analyst to assemble a deck; its agents produce the report, and every figure traces back to source data and is validated against evals built for your business, which answers finance's biggest objection to AI: whether you can defend the number to a board or an auditor. It meets teams where they work, inside ChatGPT, Claude, Slack, Teams, and email, and exports to Excel, PowerPoint, and Google Sheets. Concourse reports customer results including a 75% reduction in manual work and 20+ hours saved per user per month, is SOC 2 Type II certified, and connects to 100+ systems including NetSuite, QuickBooks, Snowflake, Salesforce, and Stripe. For the how-to, see our guide to[automated financial reporting](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/automated-financial-reporting) .


**Best for.** Finance teams that want AI agents to actually produce management, board, and variance reporting, with full traceability, rather than another tool to assemble it in.


**Keep in mind.** Concourse is built for management, board, and operational reporting, not SEC/XBRL statutory disclosure filing, that is Workiva's domain. Use Concourse for the reporting and analysis your team produces internally and for leadership.


### **2. Workiva, Best for SEC & Statutory Disclosure**


Workiva is the category leader for external and regulatory reporting: SEC filings, XBRL, and ESG and sustainability disclosure, all from a single connected, audit-ready source. If your reporting problem is the 10-K, the 10-Q, and controlled disclosure, this is the standard. Workiva is publicly traded on the NYSE under[ticker WK](https://investor.workiva.com/ir-resources/investor-faqs) and was founded in 2008 in Ames, Iowa.


**Best for.** Public companies and large enterprises whose priority is SEC, statutory, and ESG disclosure.


**Keep in mind.** It is a disclosure and controlled-reporting platform, not an FP&A or planning tool; teams looking for budgeting and forecasting reporting look elsewhere.


### **3. OneStream, Best for Enterprise Close & Consolidation**


OneStream is a unified enterprise performance management platform, strongest at financial close, consolidation, and both statutory and management reporting for large, complex organizations. Founded in 2010, it went public in 2024 and was then[taken private by Hg for $6.4 billion in a deal completed in 2026](https://www.cfodive.com/news/onestream-closes-64b-go-private-deal-hg/816799/) . It is the enterprise heavyweight for consolidated reporting.


**Best for.** Large enterprises that need consolidation, close, and reporting unified on one platform.


**Keep in mind.** It carries enterprise weight and cost, and is more than mid-market teams typically need for reporting alone.


### **4. Planful, Best for FP&A + Consolidation Reporting**


Planful is a cloud FP&A and financial performance management platform that pairs structured planning with consolidation and strong management and variance reporting across many entities. Founded in 2001 as Host Analytics and[rebranded to Planful in 2020](https://planful.com/official-planful-company-information/) , it is owned by[Vector Capital](https://www.vectorcapital.com/investments/case-study/planful) . It is a common step up for teams that need consolidation alongside their reporting.


**Best for.** Mid-market to enterprise finance teams that want FP&A, light consolidation, and management reporting together.


**Keep in mind.** Reviewers buy it for the planning-plus-consolidation combination; it is a heavier platform than a spreadsheet-native tool.


### **5. Vena, Best for Excel-Native FP&A Reporting**


Vena delivers FP&A, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting inside a familiar Excel interface, with centralized governance that removes the version-control problems of raw spreadsheets. It is a strong fit for teams that want management and board reporting without leaving Excel. Vena raised a[CAD $300M round led by Vista Equity Partners](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/55490-95) and is based in Toronto.


**Best for.** Mid-market teams committed to Excel that want governed management and board reporting.


**Keep in mind.** It is Excel-centric by design, which is the appeal for some teams and a constraint for others.


### **6. Cube, Best for Spreadsheet-Native Lean Teams**


Cube is a spreadsheet-native FP&A platform that connects Excel and Google Sheets to a centralized, governed data layer, so lean teams can run management reporting and variance analysis without leaving the spreadsheet. Founded in 2018 in New York, it raised a[Series A led by Mayfield](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/cube-software-raises-10m-series-a-to-expand-next-generation-cfo-intelligence-platform-301243447.html) and remains independent.


**Best for.** Fast-scaling startups and mid-market teams with lean FP&A that want a modern layer across Excel and Google Sheets.


**Keep in mind.** It is spreadsheet-centric, so very complex enterprise reporting can eventually outgrow it.


### **7. Datarails, Best for Excel-Centric FP&A**


Datarails automates data consolidation, reporting, and planning on top of Excel, letting teams keep their existing models while centralizing the underlying data. Founded in 2015, it raised a[$70M Series C led by One Peak at around a $550M valuation](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/sk00jsmasbl) . It is a strong management-reporting fit for Excel-first mid-market teams.


**Best for.** Excel-centric SMB and mid-market finance teams that want reporting and planning automated around their spreadsheets.


**Keep in mind.** Like other spreadsheet-native tools, very complex multi-entity reporting can push teams to a heavier platform. See our[Datarails alternatives](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/datarails-alternatives) guide for the fuller picture.


### **8. insightsoftware, Best for Operational ERP Reporting**


insightsoftware is a portfolio of Office-of-the-CFO reporting tools built by private-equity roll-up; its best-known product, Spreadsheet Server, delivers real-time operational and financial reporting straight from your ERP's general ledger (SAP, Oracle, and others) into Excel. Formed in 2018 and backed by TA Associates, Genstar, and[Hg](https://www.ta.com/news/insightsoftware-attracts-c1bn-strategic-investment-from-hg-to-continue-to-scale-as-a-platform-and-leader-in-financial-reporting-and-epm-software/) , it is a go-to for ERP-heavy finance teams.


**Best for.** ERP-centric teams that need live, drillable operational reporting out of the general ledger.


**Keep in mind.** It is a portfolio of products rather than a single platform, so scope your needs to the specific tool (e.g. Spreadsheet Server vs. Certent for disclosure).


*Also worth a look:*[Fathom](https://www.fathomhq.com/) offers lightweight management reporting for small businesses and accounting firms (now owned by The Access Group), and Wolters Kluwer's CCH Tagetik is a mature enterprise CPM platform for consolidation and statutory reporting. We kept the main list to the tools most commonly evaluated across reporting types.


## **Which financial reporting software is right for you?**


There is no single best financial reporting software, only the best fit for the report you need to produce and the team producing it.


- **Choose Concourse** if you want AI agents to *produce* management, board, and variance reporting end to end, with every number traceable and audit-ready.
- **Choose Workiva** if your priority is SEC, statutory, and ESG disclosure.
- **Choose OneStream** if you need enterprise close, consolidation, and reporting unified.
- **Choose Planful** if you want FP&A plus consolidation and management reporting together.
- **Choose Vena or Datarails** if you want governed reporting without leaving Excel.
- **Choose Cube** if you are a lean team that wants a modern spreadsheet-native layer.
- **Choose insightsoftware** if you need live operational reporting straight from your ERP.


The clearest shift in 2026 is between tools that give you a better place to *build* the report and AI agents that *produce* it for you. Most of this list is the former; the AI-agent layer is the latter, and increasingly teams pair a reporting or planning tool with an agent that generates the recurring reporting on top.


## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What is the best financial reporting software?**


It depends on the report. Workiva leads for SEC and statutory disclosure, OneStream for enterprise consolidation, Planful and Vena for FP&A and management reporting, and insightsoftware for operational ERP reporting. For teams that want AI agents to produce management, board, and variance reporting end to end with audit-ready traceability, Concourse is the strongest AI-agent option.


### **What is the best financial reporting software for small businesses?**


Smaller teams typically look at spreadsheet-native tools like Cube or Datarails, or lightweight management-reporting tools like Fathom, for quick-to-deploy reporting. Increasingly they also use AI-agent platforms like Concourse to produce recurring reporting without building and maintaining it by hand.


### **What is the best software for SEC and statutory reporting?**


Workiva is the category leader for SEC filings, XBRL, and controlled statutory and ESG disclosure. insightsoftware's Certent and Wolters Kluwer's CCH Tagetik also serve disclosure and regulatory reporting. These are distinct from FP&A and management-reporting tools.


### **How is an AI agent different from traditional financial reporting software?**


Traditional financial reporting software is where a person builds the report: it centralizes data and provides a surface to assemble it. An AI agent platform like Concourse produces the report itself, pulling the data, running the analysis, and generating the deliverable across your existing systems, with a human approving. One is where you build; the other does the work.


### **Does Concourse replace financial reporting software?**


For management, board, and variance reporting, Concourse agents can produce those outputs directly from your source data, so they can replace the manual assembly. For SEC and statutory disclosure specifically, a dedicated tool like Workiva is still the right system; teams often run Concourse for internal and management reporting alongside it.


## **The bottom line**


Financial reporting software is not one category but several, disclosure, consolidation, FP&A, and operational reporting, and the right tool depends on which report is your bottleneck. Workiva owns statutory disclosure, OneStream owns enterprise consolidation, and the Excel-native tools own mid-market FP&A reporting.


The bigger shift is from software that gives you a better place to build the report to software that produces it.
